               COMMENTS OF CENTERPOINT ENERGY HOUSTON ELECTRIC, LLC

       CenterPoint Energy Houston Electric, LLC ("CenterPoint Energy" or the "Company")

provides these comments to the Commission's Proposal for Publication of a new rule 25.521

rega rding the curtailment of transmission-voltage large load retail customers and the

development of a large load demand management service ("LLDMS") to competitively procure

demand reductions from such customers. The new rule is intended to implement the statutory

directives of PURA § 39.170 (enacted in 2025 as part of Senate Bill No. 6). CenterPoint Energy

supports the proposed rule, subject to the comments below, which cover only subsections (a)-

(c). CenterPoint Energy has no comments on subsections (d)-(i). The Company addresses the

Commission's questions included in the Proposal for Publication's preamble following its rule

comments.

A.     Subsection (a)(1) Clarifications.

       Subsection (a) of the proposed rule implements subsection (a) of PURA § 39.170, directing

the Commission to require ERCOT to ensure that each electric utility "serving a transmission-

voltage customer develops a protocol, including the installation of any necessary equipment or

technology before the customer is interconnected, to allow the load to be curtailed during firm

load shed."   The new rule mirrors the language in PURA § 39.170 in stating that this load

curtailment requirement applies only to "transmission voltage customers" who have been

"interconnected after December 31, 2025." The Company requests clarification on both phrases.



                                                1
        The term "transmission-voltage customer" has no load size reference, and the Company

believes the statute's intent is for its curtailment requirement to apply to all transmission-voltage

customers, rega rdless of load size. The Company asksthe Commission to confirm if this is correct.

Relatedly, the Company is less certain as to whether the curtailment requirement in subsection

(a) is intended to applyto all transmission-voltage customer loads, includingtransmission-voltage

wholesale storage loads and their related auxiliary retail loads, which rule 25.501(m)(2) requires

to be separately metered. The Company urges the Commission to clarify the scope of PURA

39.170(a)'s curtailment requirement in terms of both the size and types of load that it

encompasses.

       Secondly, the curtailment requirement applies only "to a load interconnected after

December 31, 2025."      The Company is uncertain when a load is considered to have been

interconnected for purposes of the applicability of this curtailment requirement. One reasonable

interpretation of when an interconnection occurs is when the point of interconnection is

energized for the commencement of commercial operations. The Company seeks Commission

clarification of when an interconnection should be deemed to have occurred.

B.     Subsection (a)(2) Effect of LLDMS on a TDU's Load Shed Obligation.

       CenterPoint Energy believes that all load that is curtailed pursuant to the LLDMS program

to be implemented by ERCOT should be counted as part of the a TDU's load shed obligation when

an EEA Level 3 load shed event occurs. In other words, the LLDMS participating customers' load

should be included in determining a TDU's load shed MW obligation.




                                                  2
 C.     Subsection (b) Definition of Transmission Emergency.

       Subsection (b) defines the term "transmission emergency" as meaning a "condition in

which an element on the transmission system is operating above its emergency rating such that

it creates a significant riskof firm load shed." However, the proposed rule does not use this term.

Question no. 4 in the Proposal for Publication preamble asks if LLDMS should be used for

transmission emergencies, anticipating that the term will be used in a future version of the

proposed rule. The Company addresses question no. 4 below.

D.     Subsection (c) Participation in LLDMS.

       Underthe proposed rule, participation in LLDMS would be limited to large load customers,

which is defined in the proposed rule as a customer with a total NCP at a single site equal to or

greater than 75 MW The proposed rule's " large load customer" definition is different from the

"large load customer" definition proposed in Project No. 58481, which expressly includes both

transmission-voltage and distribution-voltage large load customers.       The Company requests

Commission clarification on whether participation in LLDMS is intended to be limited to

transmission-voltage large load customers, or whether distribution-voltage large load customers

may also participate.

       To pre-qualify for LLDMS participation, the proposed rule also requires the large load

customer seeking to participate to "offer at least 1 MW of demand reduction." The Company

believes that a large load customer's minimum offer should be at least 10 MW. One MW is

insignificant in relation to the total NCP demand of a large load customer.




                                                3
                                  QUESTIONS FOR COMMENT

1.   Proposed subsection (f)(1)(C) authorizes payment to a qualified scheduling entity representing
     a large load customer that is not instructed by ERCOT to deploy but is subject to availability
     verification during the Large Load Demand Management Service (LLDMS) obligation period.
     Should a large load customer that is available but not ultimately instructed to deploy during the
     LLDMS obligation period be compensated some percentage of the market clearing price for the
     large load customer' s availability to reduce demand during the LLDMS obligation period? If so,
     what is an appropriate payment to the large load customer for their availability during the
     LLDMS obligation period?

     CenterPoint Energy has no comments on this question at this time.

2.   Proposed subsection (f)(4) imposes a maximum budget of $54 million in a calendar year. What
     is an appropriate budget for the LLDMS program?

     CenterPoint Energy has no comments on this question at this time.

3.   What cadence should ERCOT use to assess an extreme weather condition and how far in
     advance should ERCOT start the auction to procure LLDMS?

     CenterPoint Energy agrees with the proposed cadence described in subsection (d)(1) of the
     proposed rule.

4.   Should ERCOT be allowed to deploy LLDMS for transmission emergencies? If so, what
     limitations, if any, should the Commission impose on this authority?

     Yes, ERCOT should be allowed to deploy LLDMS for transmission emergencies, as that term is
     defined in subsection (b) of the proposed rule. However, the deployment of LLDMS for
     transmission emergencies should not be used as a permanent solution to a recurring transmission
     emergency issue.    If LLDMS is repeatedly having to be deployed for the same transmission
     emergency issue, then it means that the it should be an issue for transmission planning to solve,
     and the availability of LLDMS should not seen as a permanent solution to the issue.
